title: Heat in, no rise
hook: Keep heating a bowl of ice. Why does the thermometer refuse to move?

knows: kilojoules as a unit of energy
doesNotKnow: that during melting, heat goes into freeing molecules from the solid, with no temperature rise

misconception: Temperature always climbs while heat is added.
objective: The learner can explain that 200 kJ added to 1.0 kg of ice at 0 °C melts about 0.60 kg and leaves ice and water at 0 °C, because melting needs about 334 kJ/kg, and that only after all the ice has melted does the temperature rise (about 1 °C per 4.18 kJ).

claims.text: Melting ice needs about 334 kJ per kg.
claims.source: Enthalpy of fusion of water 333.6 kJ/kg (6.01 kJ/mol) at 0 °C (CRC Handbook, 'Properties of ice and supercooled water').

claims.text: 200 kJ added to 1.0 kg of ice at 0 °C melts about 0.60 kg and leaves about 0.40 kg of ice, all at 0 °C.
claims.source: 200 / 334 = 0.599 kg melted; none left over to warm the water (node; Demo.tsx iceLeft(), temp()). Assumes no heat lost to the surroundings and the mixture kept stirred.

claims.text: Once all the ice has melted, 1 kg of water warms by about 1 °C per 4.18 kJ; the same 200 kJ given to 1 kg of liquid water at 0 °C would warm it to about 48 °C.
claims.source: Specific heat of liquid water about 4.18 kJ/(kg K) (CRC Handbook); 200 / 4.18 = 47.8 °C (node).

claims.text: During melting, heat breaks molecules free of the ice's rigid structure without making them move faster, so the temperature holds.
claims.source: Latent heat and phase-change plateaus (Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, ch. on phase changes); temperature tracks the average kinetic energy of the molecules, which melting at fixed pressure does not raise.

claims.text: (Recall) Water boiling at 1 atm stays at about 100 °C when heated harder; the extra heat boils it away faster.
claims.source: Boiling plateau at the normal boiling point, 99.97 °C at 101.325 kPa (CRC Handbook); enthalpy of vaporisation 2,257 kJ/kg (CRC Handbook).

recall.question: A pot of water is boiling hard at 100 °C. You turn the burner up. The water's temperature…
options: stays at about 100 °C; it boils away faster
recall.why: Like melting, boiling uses the extra heat to free molecules (into steam), not to speed them up, so the temperature holds.
